steps.text: Rub horseradish mustard all over pork loin. Layer onion and apple in a slow cooker and set pork loin on top. Pour in sauerkraut and its juices. Season with salt and pepper, then add chicken broth.
Cover and cook on Low until pork is very tender, 6 to 8 hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Sauerkraut Pork Loin
raw_recipe.description: Place onion, apples, pork loin, and sauerkraut into the crockpot, add some seasonings and chicken broth, and you'll come home to a delicious dinner.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was good, but if I make it again, I would use a cut other than a pork loin. That much time in the slow cooker for the pork loin was just too much. I think it would have worked better with a pork shoulder cut (not as lean a cut of meat) intended for these longer cooking times. I would also cut back on the chicken broth to perhaps only 1/2 to 3/4 cup. The horseradish mustard gave it a nice kick. I would also sear the meat before adding it to the slow cooker (simply personal preference for a browner roast) and add a bit ot garlic and thyme to the "rub". I may try this one again with the above modifcations.

I used pork shoulder, spicy brown mustard, no apples or onions. Used my favorite spices while browning the roast before placing it in the crock pot on top of the sauerkraut and rubbed the mustard on top and sides. Instead of the broth I poured about 2/3 of a bottle of Chang beer over the top then drank the rest. After 6 or so hours on low I broke the pork up among the sauerkraut with forks and served it with garlic mashed potatoes. Absolutely delicious and couldn't be easier! Thanks!

The only things I changed in the recipe was that I braised the roast before rubbing it with the horseradish. I didn't have a granny smith apple so substituted a pink lady. I heated the chicken broth in the same pan I had braised the meat in so I could deglaze the pan and reclaim those tiny bits of deliciousness. I had started with a roast that was only partially thawed so I decided to turn the crock pot from low to high after 1 hour. It was perfectly done after a total of 6 hours.

After I made it the second time I made some changes. Used 2 onions and 2 apples, also added 2 tablespoons of Inglehoffer Cream Style Horseradish Sauce to the mustard mixed. Browned the pork loin and then spread the mustard mixture on the meat. Poured the chicken broth in before I added the meat, placed the meat on top of onions and apples, pour sauerkraut on top and cook. After it cooked I broke the meat up and then cooked some egg noodles, added the meat mixture to egg noodles and served. Was excellent and will make it again!!

I used a tenderloin marinated in a bacon/apple mixture and browned it before placing in the crock. Threw in some baby carrots last hour. Served over a Idahoan instant mashed tater applewood smoked bacon flavor!!!! OUT FLAMING STANDING!!! Thank you Jamie!!!!!

Will definitely make this again! Love reading all the reviews and what everyone changes. I placed granny Smith apple sliced on the bottom. Sea salt and pepper on my pork loin. Browned both sides. Entire bag of sauerkraut and 1/2 can of beer. Cooked 3 1/2 hours on low setting. So tender and lots of leftovers. Thanks!

WHY did I wait so long to try this recipe?! It is deceptively simple-sounding, soooo scrumptious, super easy to prepare and inexpensive (relatively!). I could not find horseradish mustard, I used a Tablespoon of yellow mustard and a Tablespoon of prepared horseradish mixed together (I could taste just a hint of the horseradish and it was delicious). The only other change I made was to sprinkle the tiniest bit of celery seed along with the salt and pepper. Just divine, thank you so much Nashville Nosher!

This recipe was really good..we loved the horseradish/mustard rub...I did braise the Pork Loin 1st then slathered on the mustard combo...delicious...also the addition of the apples...I added two chopped really made the sauerkraut delicious and I only used 3/4 cup of chicken stock....Will be making this again and again...Thanks

Delicious. Based on other reviews we added baby red potatoes to the slow cooker. We also browned the pork loin before putting it in the slow cooker and draped 3 slices of bacon on the mustard-rubbed pork loin. Our neighbor tried some and immediately asked for the recipe -nancy lee

Went even easier and used a pre-seasoned tenderloin cut in half, can of sauerkraut, and can of chicken broth. Cooked on low for 3-1/2 hours and high for the remaining 3-1/2. With an hour to go I added 1/4 C brown sugar. Was delicious and the tenderloin fell apart into shreds. Served with frozen mashed potatoes and was a no effort meal.
I used two apples and a two pound bag of sauerkraut. The loin was tender and moist. Very tasty!

Made this for our New Year’s Day Good Luck dinner. It did disappear pretty quickly. I suggest less chicken broth, maybe 1c. The pork loin was dry (surprising, since the crock pot ended up really full of liquid after cooking.) I suggest adding a little more horseradish mustard after cutting the meat up, or have it available for people to add to taste. The sauerkraut, onion and apple together was delicious! I served this recipe with garlic mashed potatoes.

If I could give this 4.5 stars I would. Next time I’ll use two apples. The sauerkraut came in two 8 oz cans and next time I’ll drain one can and keep the chicken broth at the 1/2 C I used this time. I’d like to cut down on the liquid a little and boost the chicken flavor a little. I microwaved a bag of frozen small potatoes to serve on the side. Next time some rye bread too. Overall we were pleased.
This is a great recipe. I’ve made it several times.

This was so easy to make and delicious! I used a pork shoulder and followed the recipe as written and didn’t change a thing. Next time I would reduce the liquid as it was a bit soupy but tasted wonderful. I served with with garlic mashed potatoes. Definitely a keeper and will be making it again!
Turned out excellent
This was excellent! I substituted potatoes for the apple and only used maybe 1/4 cup of broth. Will for sure be making this again! Just wish more of my family loved sauerkraut as much as I do!

I made this and it turned out to be really good. Since I live alone, I take one serving to eat immediately and freeze the rest. in one serving containers. I like the food even better as it has mingled while in the freezer. I just take a helping and microwave it.

Not good - pork was very dry, very tough and not enough flavor. I followed the recipe exactly, but wish I had tried a different cut of pork as one reviewer suggested. The sauerkraut was good though. The dogs ended up being the beneficiary of last night's meal.
